R0268.title: Robot Perception Adversarial Attack
R0268.definition: Physical-layer spoofing and jamming against robot sensors (LiDAR, IMU, camera, ultrasonic, GPS/BeiDou) that makes the perception system output distorted data, causing errors in localization, obstacle avoidance, and grasping decisions.
R0268.description:
Robot perception adversarial attacks deceive embodied-intelligence perception hardware via physical means. For LiDAR spoofing, Cao et al. (CCS 2019) used a photodiode synchronized with the victim LiDAR laser pulses to inject fake point clouds, forcing a moving autonomous vehicle to brake suddenly or freeze; NDSS 2025 research showed LiDAR object-erasure attacks succeed at over 96% at 60 km/h and 110 m distance. For IMU spoofing, Son et al. (USENIX Security 2015) used acoustic waves to disturb MEMS gyroscopes to make a drone lose control; NDSS 2023 systematized acoustic-injection attack foundations. Camera spoofing includes laser blinding and Rolling-Colors-style rolling-shutter manipulation of traffic-light recognition. For GPS/BeiDou spoofing, the UT Austin Humphreys team demonstrated in 2012 hijacking a drone's heading with sub-$1000 equipment.

This risk is a core threat to autonomous-driving and mobile-robot perception-layer security, overlapping with R0189 (sensor spoofing attack) but more focused on embodied-intelligence multi-sensor fusion systems; together with R0205 (AIoT fusion attack) it constitutes the perception-layer attack surface.
R0268.influence: Causes robots to lose localization, misidentify obstacles, deviate from trajectory, or even crash and fall; it is a core threat to autonomous-driving and mobile-robot safety, usable to cause traffic accidents, hijack drones, or paralyze warehouse logistics robots.
